subject: Terminal Delight adds an explicit offline launch for unfamiliar build scripts with one work directory and no other-pane control
reader: Parker owns Terminal Delight and knows the rogue-pane question, returning from AFK without having seen the implementation or test logs

sections.heading: Keep an unfamiliar build away from the rest of your workspace
sections.text:
A build script in an ordinary Terminal Delight pane has your account’s access, including routes to other panes. This change adds an explicit Restricted launch for offline shell/build work: the chosen project, read-only system tools and temporary home/tmp. It cannot open host controllers or new connections. Standard terminals keep their existing behavior. Online agents, TUIs and automatic handoffs are unavailable in this first profile. 
 Single owner Explicit restricted launch 0.4 unchanged

sections.heading: The question was about programs sharing one person’s authority
sections.text:
“Single user” tells us who owns the workspace. It does not tell us which program that person intended to authorize. A local socket alone cannot make that distinction. 01 · The existing Standard contract 

 Ordinary workload 
Normal account access 
 Host services, other files and processes, network 
Reachable through ordinary account authority 
 Standard remains useful for arbitrary terminal work, with ordinary account authority. A malicious Standard program can still edit state, launch another window or contact same-user services. The new global-toggle guard reduces cooperative bypass and nuisance; it is not the isolation boundary. Source: the existing host/control routes and selected threat model.

sections.heading: Restriction begins before workload code starts
sections.text:
02 · Add an OS boundary; keep the rest in place 

 Restricted workload 
One work directory · temporary home · plain text 
 Host services, other files and processes, network 
Blocked by required namespaces, descriptor cleanup and connection filtering 
 Restricted code and its children receive the chosen files, not the host’s ambient channels. Read-only system programs remain available; secrets already inside the chosen work directory are granted content. Namespace or descriptor setup failure stops the command; there is no Standard fallback. Plain-text relaying closes terminal-protocol routes. Source: the actual launch policy and OS canary tests, not a mock container design. 
Notes, terminal output and the shared work directory remain influence channels. Its authorized output can mislead a later privileged consumer. The initial scan rejects hard links, protected state/config overlaps, host sockets, pipes, devices and nested mounts; syscall filtering also blocks sockets that appear there later.

sections.heading: A useful TD action needs a narrow grant
sections.text:
03 · Add one grant, without exposing the host controller 

 Restricted workload 
One work directory · temporary home · plain text 
 Host services, other files and processes, network 
Blocked by required namespaces, descriptor cleanup and connection filtering 
 Optional own-note grant 
Preconnected typed gateway → calling pane only. Outside operator can revoke. 
 The workload can post only text on its own pane when explicitly granted. The preconnected gateway accepts no target, generic RPC, approval answer, document action or handoff. The recipient’s process generation and existing MCP switches are checked on each note. A separate outside operator channel can revoke; it cannot be reached through the workload’s files or connection API. Source: broker tests and the scratch native-window run. 04 · Authority ends without silently returning 

 Launch 
Fresh run ID.
One selected scope. 
 Request more 
One pending proposal.
No new permission. 
 Revoke 
Finish an accepted note.
Deny subsequent notes. 
 Exit / replacement 
No inherited grant.
New run required. 
 Revocation stops future TD use, not work already completed. It does not undo files, recall information or stop file work already running. Filesystem/network changes require a new launch. This profile has no automatic handoff operation. An unrestricted reader can still act on its authorized output; TD does not claim to constrain that reader. Source: lifecycle, concurrency and native revocation checks.

sections.heading: The first profile can be used today in the development build
sections.text:
05 · The implemented surface is an explicit command 

terminal-delight restricted run --workdir /path/to/project -- sh -c 'make test' 
 /work → chosen directory Network → none Home → temporary TD → none by default 
terminal-delight restricted run --workdir /path/to/project --td-note -- sh 
terminal-delight restricted call '{"op":"note","text":"Build complete"}' 
From outside, use the run ID printed at launch: 
terminal-delight restricted status RUN
terminal-delight restricted revoke RUN 
 Choose Restricted explicitly for offline work; existing panes are never retroactively certified. Add --read-only for a read-only project. TUIs, provider credentials, GUI apps and automatic agent delegation are unavailable. Programs that close inherited descriptors lose the TD channel. Linux descriptor cleanup, seccomp and the required bubblewrap options must work; unsupported setup refuses launch. The earlier GUI mockups remain planning sketches.

sections.heading: The checks include successful work and attempted escapes
sections.text:
06 · Actual evidence and honest limits | 
 | Check | Result 

 | Default terminal core · whole suite | 2652 passed · 13 ignored 
 | Fallback terminal core · whole suite | Pending 

 | Actual OS boundary | 3 probes passed: allowed build; protected files, FD, processes and services; later Unix socket; read-only work; revoke and supervisor death. 

 | Actual native window | Own note succeeded at the proven supervisor PID. Existing writes-off policy, forged target, delegation and post-revoke note were refused. Other panes unchanged. 

 | Deliberately weakened implementations | Eight module/filter mutations caught; routing/dispatch/control mutation qualification pending. 

 | Format, strict lints, optimized build, CI | Final qualification in progress; see the evidence receipt for current state. 

 | Online/TUI/GUI/automatic handoff profiles | Unavailable. No compatibility claim. 

 | Full resource quotas / hostile host / kernel | Outside this profile’s demonstrated protection. 

 A denial counts only when the boundary was reached, and allowed work still succeeds. The first tests caught a refused parent-/proc mount and a real inherited-FD escape in the implementation; both changed the design. Mutation checks then deliberately reopen those routes and must fail. Counts above include existing ignored tests; the three OS tests are separately invoked, rather than called passed because the default suite skips them. 
All adversarial work used scratch files, services and windows. No live pane or 0.4 release ref was changed. The native handoff feature retains its separate cooperative Standard contract and qualification work. 
 Source, commands and reproducible evidence 
The mechanism drawings follow the implemented policy; their geometry is illustrative. Green is a granted/verified route, blue is host structure, orange is an attempted route that is refused, grey is unavailable or unmeasured. No performance estimate is implied. 
- Launch, typed broker and filtered I/O 
- Native-ABI syscall policy 
- Real OS boundary probes 
- Selected architecture and threat model 
- Qualification receipt 
- The single security pull request 
Bubblewrap is reused as an installed mechanism, with policy owned by TD. Its upstream guidance explains that callers define protection. The descriptor mount verifies the selected directory; kernel connections and addressed sends are denied by the additional filter. No external code or prompt was copied into the implementation.
